page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with a narrow margin of notes on the right, cut off by the scan edge. Running head at the top, page number 96. Three short dialogue headings with their numbers, each followed by its text, and a speaker name at the end.

main_text.p: Quæ enim sermone peccamus, re vera luemus. Moderatam igitur feruato linguam, caueosque vt non nisi cum veritate iures: nam cum leuis res vi-deatur esse iuramentum: omni tamen onere gra-uius est. vnde Tantalus etiam punitus est, quo-niam in rebus diuinis linguæ suæ non poterat mo-derari.[illegible, ~2 letters][illegible, ~3 letters]
main_text.head: Ruff. Sevtlio Coriano. LXVIII.
main_text.p: Cepi demum peffimam vulpeculam, & captam diuerfis vinculis cuftodio fceleftiffimam, edu-camque in publicum, Coriane rufticis omnibus conuocatis, ac de hofte triumphabo. & publice ea poenas accipiet, pro multis malis vnum fubitura fupplicium.[illegible, ~2 letters][illegible, ~3 letters]
main_text.head: Amat. Calliope Laidi. LXIX.
main_text.p: Crobylo & cicada Gorgias ornatur, nondum pubescens. & ferocit propter formam, efcamque doloris proponit nobis decorem. ego vero & fe-nectam,& morbum, & triftitiam tabulis infcribi-lans, ante ianuam amentis deponam, ea enim habebit aliquando fuæ formæ decoriq; aduerfaria.[illegible, ~2 letters][illegible, ~2 letters]
main_text.head: Eth. Plato Axiocho. LXX.
main_text.p: Habenis equos dirigimus, & nauigamus alias quidem velis extendentes nauim: alias anchoris frenantes quafi retinemus. fic gubernandum lin-guam, Axioche, alias quidem fermonibus exercen-do, alias autem filentio confopiendo.[illegible, ~2 letters][illegible, ~1 letter]

page.notes: The right margin is cut off by the edge of the scan. Its note fragments (short partial words such as "Ik", "tan", "nih", "hor", "tc", "fc", "dc", "d", "q", "in") are too cropped to read, so they are marked illegible at their approximate places. The marks "\" under the last paragraph and the stray dot above it are not printed text and were left out. The line "fe-nectam" is read from a hyphenated line break and may be "fenectam" or "senectam" in the original. Possible printing or reading doubts: "edu-camque" and "fe-nectam" at line ends.
